messages:
lina: starting a quick compatibility probe for cust Stonewall's LoRA merge. base model redwood-3b, they applied a 4x LoRA patch and we quantized to int4 for cost. initial smoke shows token misalignment on currency amounts (e.g., '£1,200' -> tokenized oddly) and a soft drop in invoice extraction F1 (~4% drop).
kevin: can you paste a failing sample and the evalpack command you ran?
lina: sure — here's the command i used to run the lightweight pack:```bash
ri-cli eval run --model redwood-3b:int4 --adapter stonewall-lora --evalpack stonewall/quick-invoice-v1 --batch 32 --timeout 600
```and an anonymized sample pair:
INPUT: "Invoice total: £1,200.00 payable by 03/20."
GOLD: {"total": "1200.00", "currency": "GBP", "due": "2025-03-20"}
PRED: {"total": "1", "currency": "£", "due": "03/20"}  <-- tokenization split + parser drop
ci-bot: Test run 719000-77 completed. Metrics: extraction_f1: 0.86 (baseline 0.90), exact_match: 0.78 -> 0.74. 12/200 cases flagged as token_oddity. Logs: s3://ri-logs/7190001234/719000-77.log
sam: looks like tokenizer vocabulary mismatch between our base tokenizer and the LoRA's training tokenizer. Did they train with a different locale setup? can we get the adapter's tokenizer metadata?
lina: yeah they used a fork with additional currency tokens added (GBP_SYMBOL mapped to '£' as a single token) but during our int4 quant + runtime compile we fell back to canonical tokenizer which splits '£1,200' into ['£','1',',','200'] -> upstream parser expects ['GBP_SYMBOL','1200'] so heuristics break.
k evin: options: 1) remap tokenizer on load (preferred) 2) postprocess parser to merge currency tokens 3) re-export adapter using our canonical tokenizer. what's quickest?
rita: for customer SLA, quick mitigation = postprocess merge + short-term routing to redwood-3b:fp32 for invoice-heavy routes. longer term: remap tokenizer on load and add a unit test to evalpack.
mohit: i can patch the runtime to apply a tokenizer alias table on adapter load. simple mapping file e.g.:```json
{"GBP_SYMBOL": "£", "EUR_SYMBOL": "€"}
```this would cause the tokenizer to treat those sequences as single tokens at tokenization time. would want a config flag: adapter.token_aliases=true
lina: +1. can you throw a small heat test? run same evalpack in int4 with alias mapping enabled and compare.
ci-bot: Job queued 719000-78 by mohit. Command:```bash
ri-cli eval run --model redwood-3b:int4 --adapter stonewall-lora --evalpack stonewall/quick-invoice-v1 --config adapter.token_aliases=true --batch 32
```
ci-bot: Job 719000-78 complete. Metrics: extraction_f1: 0.895 (+0.035), exact_match: 0.785 (+0.045). Token_oddity cases reduced from 12 to 2. Artifacts: s3://ri-logs/7190001234/719000-78.log
kevin: lovely. can we add a unit in the evalpack to assert no currency token splits for top 10 locales? add a small test set and fail the pack if split occurs.
sam: i'll add a tokenizer assertion test and a tiny dataset (20 examples). i'll push to stonewall/quick-invoice-v1.
lina: plan: (1) keep int4 in prod but enable adapter.token_aliases flag for Stonewall routes, (2) add unit in evalpack, (3) schedule a follow-up to re-export adapter with canonical tokenizer for long-term. tagging @oncall for rollout window. thanks all :thumbsup:
